author: agent
objective: Among laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 cases in the four UK nations from 2020-03-26 through 2020-09-15, what is the association of daily nation-level ambient PM2.5 across the infection-course lag window with instantaneous case fatality, conditional on temperature, sunshine duration, weekday, and country effect?

scientific_invariants.research_question: Among laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 cases in the four UK nations from 2020-03-26 through 2020-09-15, what is the association of daily nation-level ambient PM2.5 across the infection-course lag window with instantaneous case fatality, conditional on temperature, sunshine duration, weekday, and country effect?
scientific_invariants.target_outcome_and_population: Back-projected COVID-19 deaths (assigned to confirmation day) out of laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 cases among residents of England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.
scientific_invariants.principal_contrast: Odds ratio for PM2.5 concentration relative to 10 µg/m³, evaluated across lag 0–10 days (virus exposure through confirmation; reported stage-specific contrast includes 19 versus 10 µg/m³ one day after symptom onset).
principal_variants: Article best model (Model 6): binomial-logit distributed-lag nonlinear PM2.5 association, jointly adjusted for distributed-lag temperature and sunshine duration, weekday, and country random effect; PM2.5 reference 10 µg/m³.
scientific_invariants.broad_geography: England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland, United Kingdom

article_evidence.finding: Methods: daily air-pollution averages were collected for every UK country from the DEFRA Air Information Resource; missing values were replaced by the prior 7-day average.

Methods/model formulation: deaths back-projected to confirmation day; D′_t^k ~ Binomial(C_t^k, pi_t^k); country random effects, weekday, distributed-lag environmental predictors; maximum lag 10 days for temperature and air pollution.
Results Tables 1–2: Model 6 with temperature, sunlight duration, and PM2.5 was selected; Figure 2 reference PM2.5 is 10 µg/m³.
Supplement contains the detailed model-selection and environmental-effect methodology.

article_evidence_map.target_discrepancy: The task target says covariates temperature, sunshine, nation; full paper additionally specifies weekday and confirms country as a random effect. Relative humidity was tested in Model 7 but Model 6 was selected, so it is not included in the primary target.
article_evidence_map.outcome_method: The exact outcome requires non-parametric back-projection with a gamma time-to-death distribution (mean 7.92 days), which will be implemented or explicitly bounded based on recoverable source detail.
